title: Reply to the ‘Comment on “The role of H 3 PO 4  in the preparation of activated carbon from NaOH-treated rice husk residue”’ by N. K. L. Hiep and V.-D. Dao,  RSC Adv. , 2026,  16 , DOI: 10.1039/D6RA05297E
content: We thank Hiep and Dao for their interest in our previous work and for raising questions regarding the high-temperature m/z = 34 signal and the associated phosphorus chemistry during H3PO4 activation. We agree that monitoring m/z = 34 alone does not provide unambiguous identification of PH3 and that this assignment should therefore be regarded as tentative. However, the quantitative comparison of uncalibrated temperature programmed decomposition-mass spectra (TPD-MS) signals presented in the Comment cannot establish molar ratios among the evolved gases, and the hydrogen-content argument is based on an incorrect assignment of the sample reported in our original article. We further clarify that neither the pathway originally proposed nor the alternative H3PO3 disproportionation pathway can be uniquely established from the available data.
